beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: After the flood, mankind tried something God had to stop. And then God started something mankind is still living inside. This is the tale of two unities.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: On the plain of Shinar, the survivors' descendants gathered with one language and one plan:

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: Go to, let us build us a city and a tower, whose top may reach unto heaven; and let us make us a name, lest we be scattered abroad upon the face of the whole earth.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Listen to the motive. Let us make US a name. Reach heaven by our own stack of bricks. It was unity, all right — unity aimed at glory without God. One language, one project, one tower of pride.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: God scattered it. Not because heaven fears tall buildings — because He had already seen where forced unity goes. One heart pointed wrong is Babel. One heart pointed right is Zion. The direction is everything.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: So God began His own unity project, and its blueprint was the exact opposite of a tower. One man. One family. One tent in the desert.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Abram of Ur — Abraham — a man who wanted righteousness more than his father's idols. His own words about what he was looking for:

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: I sought for the blessings of the fathers, and the right whereunto I should be ordained to administer the same.

beats.speaker: father
beats.text: And I will make of thee a great nation, and I will bless thee, and make thy name great; and thou shalt be a blessing: and in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Catch the reversal. Babel said: we will make us a name. God said: I will make thy name great — so that all families of the earth are blessed. That is not favoritism. It is a delivery system — one family, carrying priesthood and gospel to everybody.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: And to seal it, God asked Abraham for the hardest walk of his life — up a mountain, with his miracle son. At the last instant, heaven stayed his hand, and a ram in the thicket took Isaac's place. The whole scene was a picture, four thousand years early: another Father. Another beloved Son. Another hill — where no voice would stay the hand.

beats.speaker: father
beats.text: And in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed; because thou hast obeyed my voice.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: From Abraham's tent came Israel. From Israel, the prophets. From the prophets, the records. And from that same family line, in a stable in Bethlehem — the Seed in whom every family on earth is blessed.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: And here is where you come in. The covenant never expired. Paul said it straight:

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: And if ye be Christ's, then are ye Abraham's seed, and heirs according to the promise.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Two unities. One built a tower to make its own name great — and shattered. One followed a promise made to bless every name on earth — and it is still gathering. You are not asked to build the tower. You are invited into the tent.

card.speaker: narrator
card.text: Babel built for its own name. Abraham was blessed for yours. You are invited into the tent.
